text:
Lena (Eng - Berlin): hey team — quick heads up: I'm moving from Berlin to Dublin at the end of April (returning from parental leave early). Need to confirm payroll cutover timing, WFH stipend continuity, and if my move creates an Irish tax/VAT presence for Redwood. Marta (People Ops): congrats! :tada: we can help. main things: payroll entity switch, benefits enrollment window, and stipend proration. When's your official relocation date?
Lena (Eng - Berlin): 2026-05-01 is the target. still finishing paperwork for the apartment. parental leave ends 2026-04-20 so there's a short overlap before move.
Marta (People Ops): perfect — that gives us time. immediate asks for you: 1) confirm move date, 2) passport/visa if non-EU, 3) Irish bank account (preferred but not required at cutover). we'll open a relocation case.
Tom (Finance): fyi — when someone moves intra-EU we usually change payroll entity on the first of a month to keep social/tax records clean. cutover 2026-05-01 looks doable.
Lena (Eng - Berlin): will my Redwood WFH stipend continue? I bought a standing desk while in DE.
Marta (People Ops): stipend policy: recurring WFH allowance continues if you're still eligible in new country, but we need to confirm local benefits and whether any one-off equipment payments are considered taxable in Ireland. we'll check.
Priya (Payroll): note — equipment single-payouts processed in DE payroll will be taxed per German rules. if we process new payments after cutover via our Irish payroll, Irish tax rules may apply. might need a gross-up to match previous net.
Lena (Eng - Berlin): ugh ok. i paid for the desk myself and claimed via expense last month.
Marta (People Ops): two paths: A) keep the DE expense as-is (no change) and issue continuation stipend from Ireland going forward; B) if you need compensation for additional costs, we can run a one-off via Irish payroll with a gross-up. what do you prefer?
Lena (Eng - Berlin): probably keep the DE claim as-is. then continue allowance in Ireland. what about benefit enrollment?
Marta (People Ops): you'll get a new benefits packet for Ireland — health plan options differ. you have a 30-day window post-cutover to enroll.
EU Legal: flag: company having an employee resident and working in Ireland typically creates a local employee presence but not automatic corporate tax nexus. however VAT/registered establishment questions depend on customer-facing activity and local contracting; for single headcount it's usually not enough to register for Irish VAT, but Finance should confirm with local counsel if you start hiring or signing contracts there.
Tom (Finance): we'll run the nexus checklist. Lena, can you confirm whether you'll sign any client contracts or meet customers in Ireland?
Lena (Eng - Berlin): not for now, just internal product work.
Priya (Payroll): workflow outline (short): 1) submit relocation form to People Ops 2) People Ops raises payroll transfer ticket 3) Payroll issues final DE payslip and starts Irish onboarding 4) benefits enrollment link sent 5) verify bank/ID 6) first Irish pay goes out on next Irish payroll date after cutover.
Marta (People Ops): submitting relocation form: https://hr.redwood.example/relocate (internal). please attach: passport scan, apartment lease or intent letter, and preferred cutover date.
Lena (Eng - Berlin): done, submitted now.
PeopleOpsBot: "Case #R-4821 created. Assigned to Marta. Reminder: payroll cutover SLA 7 business days for EU intra-entity transfers."
Marta (People Ops): quick note on WFH stipend proration: recurring monthly allowance is pro-rated by calendar days in the month under whichever payroll entity is paying. so if your cutover is 2026-05-01, May stipend will be fully paid from Irish payroll. if cutover were mid-month we'd prorate.
Lena (Eng - Berlin): thanks. any action I need on the tax side?
Tom (Finance): we'll send a short questionnaire about your residency start date and confirm any German exit tax reporting. you may need to file a German tax return for the year of move.
EU Legal: also check PRSI/social contributions timing; Ireland has separate employee/employer rates and entitlements (e.g., social insurance).
Priya (Payroll): last practical: please add your Irish personal PPS number once you have it to your employee profile; we'll update tax codes.
Lena (Eng - Berlin): got it. one more — does Redwood reimburse relocation shipping?
Marta (People Ops): yes, there's a relocation policy. shipping under a threshold is reimbursed via expense; over threshold we handle via relocation vendor. please attach shipping estimates to the case.
Lena (Eng - Berlin): perfect, thanks everyone!
Marta (People Ops): i'll follow up with a checklist in this thread and ping you 2 business days before cutover.
Tom (Finance): i'll start the nexus checklist and loop in external tax counsel if needed.
EU Legal: will review contract exposure but doesn't look like signing activity today.
PeopleOpsBot: "Reminder: benefits enrollment window opens 2026-05-02 and closes 2026-06-01 for this case."
Marta (People Ops): closing note — for parental leave continuity: request a leave handoff form so payroll knows to continue statutory payments through cutover; we'll coordinate with Payroll.
Lena (Eng - Berlin): thanks all — really appreciate the fast help :heart:
